title: Notes cannot be opened by keyboard: list rows are unfocusable li elements with a click handler on the ul
evidence: The li has no tabindex, no button or link, no role and no key handler (app.js:10, listener at app.js:30-33). The selected row is shown only by a background class, with no aria-current.
failing_case: With the keyboard only, Tab goes from search to New note to the title field. There is no stop on any note, so the user can never open a note other than the one auto-opened at load. The main task is blocked (WCAG 2.1.1, level A).
remediation: Render each row as a <button> (or a link) inside the li with the title as its name, and set aria-current="true" on the open note. Keep the click handler on the ul, which then receives keyboard activation.

title: Delete is permanent, one click, with no confirm or undo, and is a mouse-only unnamed div
evidence: removeNote calls deleteNote and persist immediately (app.js:23-28). The control is a div with an emoji, so it has no role, no accessible name and no tabindex. styles.css:12 hides it with opacity 0 until the row is hovered.
failing_case: A mouse user mis-clicks the trash icon at the right edge of a row: the note is gone from storage with no way back. A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot reach delete at all (WCAG 2.1.1, level A, and 4.1.2). A touch user has no hover, so the icon is invisible, though still tappable by accident.
remediation: Use <button type="button" aria-label="Delete note: TITLE"> that is always visible (or revealed on :focus-within as well as :hover). Add a confirm step or an 'Undo' toast that keeps the removed note for several seconds.

title: With no selected note the editor still accepts typing, and the text is lost with an uncaught TypeError
evidence: On first run (notes = []) and after deleting the open note, currentNote is null, but #title and #body stay enabled. removeNote does not clear the fields. The input listener calls scheduleSave, whose timer dereferences currentNote.title (store.js:16).
failing_case: First run: type in the body textarea. After 500 ms the timer throws 'Cannot set properties of null' and nothing is stored, while the hint still says 'Changes save automatically'. Delete the open note: its title and body remain on screen, and any further typing throws the same way and is lost.
remediation: In removeNote, clear and disable the editor when currentNote becomes null. Disable the fields until a note is open. Guard scheduleSave against a missing target. Show an empty state with a 'Create your first note' button.

title: maximum-scale=1 blocks pinch zoom on touch devices
evidence: The viewport meta caps zoom at 1. The layout is also fixed at 1200px (styles.css:2).
failing_case: A low-vision user on a phone cannot enlarge the page, and the 12px hint and 16px text stay at their size. This fails WCAG 1.4.4 (resize text, AA).
remediation: Use content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" and no maximum-scale or user-scalable=no.

title: Title input and body textarea have no label; search uses its placeholder as the only name
evidence: index.html:13 (search), 19 (title) and 20 (body textarea) have no <label>, no aria-label and no aria-labelledby. The title and body have no placeholder either.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'edit multiline text' for the editor fields, so the user cannot tell which is the title and which is the body (WCAG 3.3.2 and 4.1.2, level A). The search name disappears as soon as the user types.
remediation: Add visible <label for> elements for title and body (or at least aria-label) and a label or aria-label for search. Give the list a heading or aria-label.

title: Unguarded JSON.parse at load, and no shape check, can brick the app
evidence: The parse is at top level of store.js with no try/catch. app.js then calls n.title.toLowerCase() (app.js:6) on every record without checking that it has a title.
failing_case: localStorage 'notes' is '{bad' (truncated write, a manual edit, another app on the same origin): store.js throws at load, app.js never runs, and the page is dead with no message. If it is '[{"id":1}]' (an older record without a title) or '{}' (not an array), renderList throws on the first render and the whole app is dead on every load.
remediation: Wrap the parse in try/catch. Validate that the result is an array and normalise each record (string id, string title and body, numeric updated). On failure keep a backup copy of the raw value and start empty with a visible notice. Store a schema version.

title: No flush on pagehide or beforeunload, so the last 500 ms of typing is dropped
evidence: The only write path for edits is the debounce timer. grep shows no pagehide, beforeunload or visibilitychange handler in any file.
failing_case: Type a sentence into the body and close or refresh the tab (or the phone browser backgrounds and kills it) within half a second. The timer never fires and the sentence is not in localStorage on reload.
remediation: Add a flush() that cancels the timer and persists synchronously, and call it on pagehide and visibilitychange (hidden).

title: The debounced save writes to whatever note is current when the timer fires
evidence: scheduleSave (store.js:13-21) captures nothing at schedule time. The timer reads currentNote and the DOM fields 500 ms later. openNote (app.js:16-21) replaces both the editor values and currentNote synchronously.
failing_case: Open note A and type in the body. Within 500 ms click note B. openNote(B) overwrites the editor with B's text and sets currentNote = B. The timer then copies B's text onto B and stamps B's updated time. A's edit is never written and is lost. The same thing happens when New note is clicked within 500 ms of typing: the unsaved edit to the previous note is dropped.
remediation: Capture the target note at schedule time (const target = currentNote and the values at that moment). Flush the pending save synchronously inside openNote and createNote before switching.

title: Each tab writes its whole in-memory array, so a second tab overwrites the first's notes
evidence: notes is read once at load (store.js:2) and persist() always writes the entire array. There is no 'storage' event listener and no re-read before writing.
failing_case: Open the app in tabs A and B. In B create and fill a note. In A, edit any existing note. A's save writes its stale array and the note created in B disappears from storage, permanently.
remediation: Re-read and merge by id before writing, or listen for the 'storage' event and reload state. Per-note keys also remove the whole-array overwrite.

title: Storage write failures are swallowed while the UI says 'Changes save automatically'
evidence: persist() catches every error from localStorage.setItem and does nothing. Neither store.js nor app.js reports a result, and index.html:21 promises auto-save.
failing_case: Storage is full, or the browser is in a mode that blocks localStorage writes, so setItem throws QuotaExceededError. The user keeps typing and creating notes, the hint stays unchanged, and on the next load everything since the failure is gone.
remediation: Make persist return success or failure. On failure show a persistent, announced message such as 'Could not save: storage is full. Export your notes or free space', and keep the unsaved state marked as dirty.

title: Fixed 1200px container and 300px list column; the page scrolls sideways on phones and at 200% zoom
evidence: styles.css:2 sets a fixed width and styles.css:7 sets grid-template-columns: 300px 1fr. There is no media query. The textarea is fixed at 400px high (styles.css:14). Traced; the browser could not be driven.
failing_case: At a 390px viewport the content is 1200px wide, so the user must pan sideways to reach the editor. At 200% zoom on a 1360px window the effective viewport is 680 CSS px, also too narrow. This fails WCAG 1.4.10 (reflow, AA).
remediation: Use max-width: 1200px; width: 100%; padding: 0 16px. Below about 640px switch .layout to one column (grid-template-columns: 1fr) with the list above the editor.

title: The focus indicator is removed from every control and nothing replaces it
evidence: No :focus-visible rule exists anywhere in styles.css. The inputs have a 1px #eee border (styles.css:13) that is also invisible against white.
failing_case: Tab through the page: focus moves between search, New note, title and body with no visible change, so a keyboard user cannot tell where they are (WCAG 2.4.7, AA).
remediation: Delete the rule. Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px } for all controls.

title: Hint (#ccc) and rank (#bbb) text on white are far below 4.5:1
evidence: Calculated from the WCAG relative-luminance formula: #bbb on #fff is about 1.9:1 (styles.css:11), and #ccc on #fff is about 1.6:1 (styles.css:15). Both are small text, and the only 'saved' status is #ccc at 12px.
failing_case: A user with low vision or in sunlight cannot read 'Changes save automatically' or the #rank numbers (WCAG 1.4.3, AA).
remediation: Use at least #595959 for the hint and rank on white (7:1), and keep the 12px floor or raise it to 14px.

title: Note titles and shared-note titles are written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: renderList builds HTML from n.title (app.js:11) and the search handler builds it from s.title returned by /api/shared (app.js:46). Neither goes through an escape function or textContent. Traced; the browser could not be driven in this session.
failing_case: Type as a note title. After the 500 ms save the title is stored, and the next renderList (any search keystroke, open, delete) injects the element and runs the handler. The payload also runs on every page load, because it is persisted. A shared note whose title is that string, returned by /api/shared, executes in every other user's page the moment they search. That makes it stored XSS across users.
remediation: Create elements with document.createElement and set textContent, or pass every interpolated value through one escapeHtml helper. Do this at both sinks (app.js:11 and app.js:46), and remove the inline onclick.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: renderList re-sorts the whole array for every row, and rebuilds the list with innerHTML +=
evidence: The sort and indexOf at app.js:8-9 sit inside shown.forEach, so each render costs O(n² log n). app.js:10 appends to list.innerHTML, so the already-built DOM is re-serialised and re-parsed for every row (another O(n²)). renderList runs on every search keystroke and on every open.
failing_case: At 500 notes, each search keystroke runs 500 sorts of 500 elements and 500 re-parses of a growing list. At 5,000 notes the typing in the search box visibly stalls. The re-parse also drops any state held on the existing nodes.
remediation: Sort once outside the loop and build a Map id -> rank. Build the rows with a DocumentFragment (or one joined string) and assign once. Debounce the search input.

title: Clicking a shared-note row throws: the row has no data-id
evidence: Shared rows are <li class="shared"> with no dataset (app.js:46), and the list click handler matches any li. Number(undefined) is NaN, notes.find returns undefined, and openNote then reads currentNote.title (app.js:18).
failing_case: Search for anything that returns a shared note and click it: Uncaught TypeError, and currentNote becomes undefined. The editor keeps the previous note's text, and the next edit throws in the save timer (store.js:16).
remediation: Handle shared rows explicitly (a read-only view or a copy-to-my-notes action), or have the click handler ignore li elements without data-id. Make openNote return when the note is not found.

title: Shared-notes search has no debounce, ignores stale responses, and hides failures
evidence: Every keystroke fires a request. After the await, results are appended to #list whatever the input says now (app.js:46). res.ok is not checked, and failures only go to console.log (app.js:47).
failing_case: Type 'ab'. The response for 'a' arrives after the response for 'ab'. The list then shows the 'ab' results followed by the 'a' results. Responses for the same query can also append twice. If the server returns 500 or a 404 HTML page, res.json() throws, the user sees nothing, and cannot tell 'no shared notes' from 'search broken'. Every keystroke also sends the user's partial search text to the server.
remediation: Debounce, keep a request counter or AbortController and drop stale responses, check res.ok, and show 'Shared notes unavailable' in the UI. Render the shared section as its own container so a re-render replaces it.

quote: const note = { id: Date.now(), title: 'Untitled', body: '', updated: Date.now() };
title: Date.now() as the note id can collide
evidence: createNote uses a millisecond clock as the key, and deleteNote filters by id (store.js:30), so equal ids behave as one note. There is no uniqueness check.
failing_case: Two createNote calls within the same millisecond (a double-activated button, a script or an automated test) give both notes the same id. openNote(id) then always finds the first of them, and deleting either deletes both.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() (or a counter persisted with the data), and reject duplicates on load.

title: The list is never re-rendered after a save, so titles and #rank go stale
evidence: The save timer updates the title and the updated time and calls persist(), but never renderList. renderList runs only on open, delete and search.
failing_case: Click New note, type 'Groceries' as the title. The list keeps showing 'Untitled' until the user searches, switches notes or deletes something. The '#rank' badges also do not change after the edit that changes the order.
remediation: Call renderList (with the current filter) after the save, or update the single row. Keep the store and the view separate by emitting a change event.

quote:
✨ Welcome to NoteMaster

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Placeholder Latin and 'Welcome to' hero copy shipped on the main screen
evidence: index.html:11. The hero adds 60px of padding above the toolbar (styles.css:3), pushing the actual tool down the screen.
failing_case: Every user reads 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' as the product tagline.
remediation: Replace it with a one-line description of what the app does, or remove the hero and show the toolbar first.

title: No empty state: first run and no-match searches show a blank list with no next step
evidence: renderList writes nothing when there are no notes or no matches. No copy is rendered for either case.
failing_case: A new user sees a hero, an empty left column and an editor that does nothing (see the null-currentNote finding). Searching for text that matches nothing also shows a blank list.
remediation: Render 'No notes yet. Select New note to start.' and 'No notes match "q"' as list content.
